title: How do we fill the missing cells of the table?
description: A table has five numbers across the top and five down the side, and every cell holds the top number divided by the side number. The video fills the empty cells from three given cells, using the fact that moving the point by one place makes a quotient ten times bigger or smaller.
teaching_notes: One idea: dividing the top number by ten divides the quotient by ten, and dividing the side number by ten multiplies the quotient by ten. Ask the class which way the quotient moves when the top number becomes ten times smaller before any work is shown. Watch for students who move the quotient the same way for the top and the side numbers.

source: End of chapter Figure it Out, Q9
video_script.why: The child has seen that moving the decimal point in the numbers of a product moves the product in step, and now sees what moving the point does to a quotient, across a whole table.
video_script.substitution: The top number and the side number of a cell each move by a power of ten from the first row and column, and the quotient moves with them.
video_script.anchor: A table of cells, top numbers 1517, 151.7, 15.17, 1.517, 15170 and side numbers 37, 3.7, 0.37, 0.037, 370, with three cells already given
video_script.payoff_line: Every cell of the table is filled by moving the first quotient with the same two rules

final_answer.spoken: the five rows of the table, filled cell by cell

maths_rules: top number divided by 10 makes the quotient divided by 10; the last column 15170 = 1517 x 10 makes it x 10
side number divided by 10 makes the quotient x 10; the last row 370 = 37 x 10 makes it divided by 10
video_script.design: One idea: a move of the point in the top number or the side number moves the quotient by the same number of places, the top the same way and the side the opposite way. The table stays on the board all video; the working band gives the two rules, then fills the first row, then the other rows, and checks against a given cell.
open_questions: The book names the top and side numbers a and b. The video says the top number and the side number, so no letters are spoken.

<bookmark mark='last'/>The last side number is ten times the first one, so its quotient is ten times smaller.
